1. INTRODUCTION
Zameen ACE Mall is a mixed use development being constructed at DHA Phase-II, Islamabad.
The fourteen (14) storied structure is planned to comprise of multiple basements with maximum
excavation below existing ground level (EGL) of around 65 ft depth. The piling contractor which
has already been mobilized at site has encountered soil strata which is significantly different
from the one reported in geotechnical investigations report. A reassessment of geotechnical
characterization is sought by the client. Besides, an initial review of existing shoring system has
revealed several technical deficiencies in the design which render the existing design to be
unsafe. Further, the current design does not take into account possible water ingress during
excavation works and a comprehensive strategy to control the ground water inflow into the
excavation needs to be carried out.
M/s Birudo Engineers (BE) have been invited by the client to submit a proposal to undertake
the aforementioned services. The following sections of this document summarize TECHNICAL
and FINANCIAL details of our proposal.

2. CONSULTANT PROFILE
Consultant is a group of experts from diverse engineering backgrounds and is providing
consultancy as well as turnkey solutions to Civil, Geotechnical and Soil-Structural Interaction
issues faced by different Clients. A pool of highly qualified and experienced professionals enable
consultant to give tailor made and best engineering solutions that are successfully implied on
previous projects. Our Company Profile showcasing our complete portfolio as well as our
previously completed projects is attached as Appendix-A to this document.

Doc. Code: BE-424/R01

3. SCOPE OF SERVICES
Major activities envisaged for the project are listed below;





Confirmatory geotechnical investigations
Design of shoring system
Installation of piezometers
Design of dewatering system

Brief description of step by step activities is described in the following sections;
3.1. FIELD WORKS



DRILLING of six (06) boreholes down to a maximum depth of 60 m below existing
ground level (EGL) using hydraulic feed straight rotary drilling rig. The actual depth of
boreholes shall however be decided based upon the encountered strata so as to avoid
puncturing any undesired water aquifer beyond the depth of interest.



Performance of STANDARD PENETRATION TESTS (SPTs) in overburden soils @ 1.0 m
depth interval wherever possible,



Collection of DISTURBED AND UNDISTURBED SOIL SAMPLES from the boreholes
through Split Spoon/ Shelby/Denison tube samplers,



Installation of PIEZOMETERS in each of the encountered aquifer (i.e., installation of
double piezometers in the boreholes). The piezometers shall be so installed so that the
same

piezometers

may

be

used

to

monitor

ground

water

levels

during

excavation/dewatering works,



Determination of PIEZOMETERIC HEAD in each piezometer and recording their
variation over time.

3.2. LABORATORY WORKS
Subsequent to field investigations, all the soil and groundwater samples shall carefully be
transported to soil testing laboratory. Laboratory works would include the performance of
detailed LABORATORY TESTING on selected soil and groundwater samples to obtain the
followings;


Soil classification,



Index properties,



Strength and chemical characteristics.

Doc. Code: BE-424/R01

4

Zameen Ace Mall, DHA Phase-II, Islamabad
|Proposal for Geotechnical Consultancy Services|

To accomplish above, the following tests shall be performed on selected soil and groundwater
samples;


Sieve Analysis,



Hydrometer Analysis,



Atterberg Limits,



Specific Gravity,



Natural Moisture Content,



Bulk Density,



Consolidation,



Direct Shear,



Unconfined Compression Tests,



Sulphate, Chloride, Organic matter content in the soil,



Chemical analysis of water samples i/c Cl, SO4 & pH.

All the tests shall be performed in accordance with relevant ASTM/British Standards.
3.3. GEOTECHNICAL INVESTIGATIONS REPORT
A reassessment of the sub-soil conditions is sought by the client since the soil conditions
encountered in the initial piling bores is significantly different from the one reported in
geotechnical report of M/s Geo Crust. The nature and strength characteristics of sub-soils need
to be established accurately in order to re-assess the suitability of already proposed foundation
system. Evaluation of sub-surface water flow conditions also need to be performed in the
executed boreholes so as to design an efficient dewatering system. A detailed report on
geotechnical investigations shall be prepared in the light of field and laboratory data collected
herein and would comprise the following;



Executive summary,



Project outline along with a summary of executed field and laboratory works,



Maps (site vicinity map and investigation map),



Field logs,



Results of in-situ and laboratory testing,



Topographic, geological and seismic information pertinent to the proposed project site,

Doc. Code: BE-424/R01

5

Zameen Ace Mall, DHA Phase-II, Islamabad
|Proposal for Geotechnical Consultancy Services|



Cross-sectional profiles of sub-surface soil layers,



Recommendations for the type of cement to be used based upon chemical analysis,



Engineering analysis and recommendation for foundation(s),



Recommendations for soil improvement (where applicable),



Geotechnical consideration related to the construction of shallow foundations and pile
foundations,



Site photographs showing field works.

3.4. DESIGN OF SHORING SYSTEM
The current design of shoring system has been assessed and found to be technically deficient
which can cause serious safety hazards during excavation works. Besides, the current
configuration of ground anchors is not technically viable because of underground water flow
conditions in the subject area. A revised shoring system comprising contiguous piles, ground
anchors, soil berms, and other restraining components would therefore be designed and the
activity would include the following major components.



Design of shoring piles (geotechnical design + structural design)



Design of anchors and other restraining components including design of all connection
details (geometric design + structural design)



Design of a systematic excavation plan



Design of capping beam and wale supports

3.5. DESIGN OF DEWATERING SYSTEM
Boreholes drilled for pile construction have revealed presence of at least two ground water
aquifers at around 20 ft and 45 ft depth from existing ground level (EGL). The water aquifers
are likely to be confined in nature as observed from the gushing waterflow in the piling
boreholes. A systematic dewatering system would therefore be required to excavate down to the
required foundation level. The design of dewatering system would, in general, involve sump pits,
drainage channels, well-points, observation wells, pumps, delivery housing, etc.

Doc. Code: BE-424/R01

ABOUT US
We are a Civil Engineering Consulting Firm, offering state of the art and
state of the practice engineering solutions with our team of highly
qualified, competent and seasoned professionals. Our team possesses vast
experience of handling civil engineering design, management and
execution of projects included but not limited to Buildings, Roads,
Highways, Bridges, Power Plants, Dams and Military Facilities, etc. Our
core expertise includes Geotechnical Investigations, In-situ Geotechnical
and Geophysical Testing and Surveys, Geotechnical Design (Foundations,
Dams, Levees, Embankments, Retaining Systems, Machine Foundations,
Vibration Control in Foundations, etc.), Construction of Cast In-Place
Concrete Piles, Topographic Surveys, Value Engineering, Ground
Improvement Works, Highway Design, Traffic Engineering, Pavement
Performance Evaluation, etc.

We consider ourselves as a ‘Client-Driven’ organization by ensuring the
requirements and benefits of Clients as our top priority. We strive to
provide our valued Clients with the international level optimal
engineering solutions by making full use of hard and soft tools (i.e.,
equipment and software). All of this is done while maintaining highest
international standards of health, safety and environmental protection.

QUALITY POLICY

81

We, at BIRUDO ENGINEERS, are committed to provide quality
Design and Engineering Consultancy services with professionalism
and dedication to the complete satisfaction of our Clients. The quality
of our services is sustained through enhancement of technical knowhow and proficiency of our staff. We allocate adequate resources for
project implementation and seek improvement through a continuous
system of Monitoring and Evaluation.
In general, a Site Manager, mainly a Civil Engineer, is responsible for
overall Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC) of the
project

by

assuring

the

compliance

of

approved

working

methodology/project specifications, relevant international standards
i.e., ASTM/BS/AASHTO or whichever is applicable. In addition, to
meet the designated timelines, project progress is tracked by making
daily/weekly or monthly progress or other project specific required
reports, based on the volume of the works.

82

HSE POLICY

83

We, BIRUDO ENGINEERS, believe and continually strive for improving the
quality of our services and products while protecting people and the environment.
This commitment is in the best interests of our customers, our employees and
contractors, all stockholders, and communities in which we live and work by
committing;



Protect, and strive for improvement of, the health, safety and security of
our people always;



Eliminate Quality non-conformances and HSE accidents;



Meet specified customer requirements and ensure continuous customer
satisfaction;



Set Quality & HSE performance objectives, measure results, assess and
continually improve processes, services and product quality, through the
use of an effective management system;



Plan for, respond to and recover from any emergency, crisis and business
disruption;



Minimize our impact on the environment through pollution prevention,
reduction of natural resource consumption and emissions, and the
reduction and recycling of waste;



Apply our technical skills to all HSE aspects in the design and engineering
of our services and products;



Communicate openly with stakeholders and ensure an understanding of
our QHSE policies, standards, programs and performance. Reward
outstanding QHSE performance;



Improve our performance on issues relevant to our stakeholders that are
of global concern and on which we can have an impact, and share with
them our knowledge of successful QHSE programs and initiatives.

We are committed to continually review our policies to ensure ongoing suitability.
The commitments listed are in addition to our basic obligation to comply with all
applicable laws and regulations where we operate. This is critical to our business
success because it allows us to systematically minimize all losses and adds value

84
